items.a: Not one agent and one task — orchestrating **multiple agents across multiple workspaces** while you voice-prompt, add context, and walk away. Stack behind an **$18K MRR / $74K gross-volume** business, live-building BridgeBench V3 without manually writing code.

items.q: What is the minimum tool trio?
items.a: **Agentic IDE** + **voice-to-text** + **screenshot annotation**. Power-user stack (~12–16 hr/day): ~**$200/mo Claude**, OpenAI/Codex, Cursor, Perplexity — budget-flexible; not all required.

items.q: How many agents for a level-1 task?
items.a: Button color or copy: **one agent, no plan**, voice prompt only.

items.q: What does a level-10 AWS build look like?
items.a: Full VPC/ECR/ECS/RDS: **plan mode + five sub-agents**, Claude Code Extra High, AWS CLI profile on the machine. Level 5–6 NestJS+auth: plan mode, single strong model (**GPT-5.5 Extra High** for backend).

items.q: How does he route models by task type?
items.a: **Claude Opus 4.8** for UI design; **GPT-5.5 Extra High** for backend; separate agent for test framework — parallel tracks on non-overlapping scopes.

"If you only are working on a singular task, you're **not a really good vibe coder**." Parallel API vs UI vs tests; merge conflicts rare when scopes differ. **Git worktrees** help when needed but are often overkill.
"It allows you to literally just be able to **walk away**" — 30–60 min on infra provisioning. Deep-dive agents (~**5–10 min** autonomous research) before landing-page implementation.

items.q: What do Bridge Voice and Bridge Shot do?
items.a: **Bridge Voice**: speak prompts + save history for reuse. **Bridge Shot**: screenshot + arrow annotation into the agent — "it will cut down on **hallucinations so much**" (demo: search bar added correctly).

items.q: How should you structure the workspace?
items.a: Monorepo-style parent with **separate project directories** (API, UI, MCP); `@`-reference so agents load the right files. Cross-project refs accelerate greenfield ("reference Vibe Academy API for **Drizzle ORM** pattern").

items.q: How does Discord OAuth get set up without manual clicking?
items.a: Agent writes a **handoff prompt** for Comet browser AI → Control Browser → Discord Developer Portal app created automatically; then wire frontend ↔ API.

"Typically, when you are pushing stuff to production, it **won't necessarily work the first time**." Paste logs + screenshots back to the agent → fix pushed to main. Live outcome: Postgres RDS, NestJS auth, Docker/ECR/ECS, Discord OAuth, Vercel UI on bridgebench.ai.
